packageRules.description: Zero-manual-work policy: every workload tracks the latest published version, majors included. The e2e smoke suite is the safety net — a break becomes a new test, never a pinned-back version. Renovate opens and auto-merges the bump once CI is green.
Placeholder images in illustrative code (ghcr.io/example/*, ghcr.io/acme/*) carry no real tags — never look them up.
tik and the kurly library ship calendar-versioned tags (YYYY.M.D), which the default docker versioning cannot order.

customManagers.description: Every workload's default image. The PRIMARY image of each stage lives in its own dedicated file (workloads/<name>/<stage>.image), and any secondary image (a sidecar's, a README deploy example's) in that workload's own .libsonnet or README. catalog.json carries the SAME reference under each stage's `runs.image`, derived by rendering the stage — so it is matched here too and a bump updates both in ONE pull request, since Renovate branches per dependency and version. Regenerating the catalog is not needed: the value is the same string, not a computation over it. The placeholder registries are disabled in packageRules above.

Operator-backed workloads (mysql/mongodb/opensearch/cassandra clusters) pin a VERSION the operator maps to a container image, not a full image ref. Track each through a `// renovate: datasource=... depName=... versioning=...` hint above its `<name>Version='X'` line in the workload's own .libsonnet — a per-workload file, so these bumps never collide either.

The nginx image the examples and docs render with, so the illustrative manifests never pin a stale tag. Placeholder images (ghcr.io/acme/*, ghcr.io/example/*) carry no real tags and are deliberately not matched.
Alpine.js, fetched by gen-docs-data at docs-build time from the pinned version so the assembler page always ships the tracked release.
Operator versions the e2e scenarios install, pinned in hack/smoke/*.sh via a `# renovate:` comment above a `<TOOL>_VERSION="..."` line.

cassandra-cluster's catalog entry states the version its operator resolves to an image; the pin itself lives in the workload's own file, tracked above. Anchored on the stage's importPath, which is what names the workload in the rendered JSON.

catalog.json publishes each reference's digest beside it, so a consumer never parses one. Anchored on the image line that follows it, which is what names the dependency.
The same for the published tag, anchored on the image line that precedes it.
